mode: Success falls steeply with coherent, non-splittable task length (long dependent chains)

evidence.finding: Success falls roughly linearly in log(human task time): y=-0.07x+0.66, R^2 0.83.
80% time horizons are 4-6x shorter than 50% horizons.
A task is a coherent unit that cannot be split; 1000 one-hour problems is a 1-hour task done 1000 times.
Long-horizon Harbor tasks: best model 28.3% at R>=0.95; mean over 17 models 6.4%; 62.8% of runs get partial credit.
Median successful run finishes after 57 min; 42% of solves come after the 1-hour checkpoint.
Horizon H_s = ln(s)/ln(p); per-step accuracy falls as errors accumulate in context (self-conditioning).

how_to_use: Make the core work a chain of 6-12 dependent stages where each stage's input comes from the previous stage's verified output. Do not count independent repeats as length.

mode: Premature completion: claiming done without checking (false finish)

evidence.finding: Premature task abandonment = 16 of 32 o1 failures and 8 of 31 GPT-4 failures; defined as submitting without checking correctness.
124 self-terminated runs; 14 had R>=0.75 and stopped with ~20 min left (e.g. seven models stopped at R 0.80-0.87 on one task).
Fast models often claim completion long before they finish.
Agents did not always use the provided validation server; gpt-4o AIDE made a submission 70.7% of the time but a valid one only 54.9%.
Execution and verification errors (unaware of termination, weak verification) are TB2 failure classes.

how_to_use: State the full acceptance criteria, give a validator that checks only format (and say so), and weight the checks that a first-pass solution misses.

mode: Composing individually documented features fails (feature isolation)

evidence.finding: HTTP server: 100% visible per-feature tests vs 25% held-out composition tests.
Visible-vs-held-out gaps of roughly 32-64 pp; gap grows ~27-28 pp per 10x LOC (paper is internally inconsistent on the exact figure).
Adding composition tests to the visible set did not reliably close the gap: compositions are genuinely difficult.
Requirements met fall from 44.80% (independent) to 28.96% (dependency-aware) for GPT-Pilot.
Success declines sharply as the number of files touched rises.

how_to_use: Document every rule and the combination semantics (precedence table); put most grading weight on hidden cases that combine 2-4 documented rules, plus error paths.

mode: Standard or memorised approach is insufficient; an algorithmic insight or reformulation is needed

evidence.finding: Adding a 'dominant algorithmic lift' cut the Hard split mean pass@1 from 87.0% to 45.7%; GPT-5.4 94.8% to 49.7%.
No novel algorithms found; speedups were surface-level (better library call, parameters, Numba).
Agents tried lightly modified transformers 84% of the time where transformers work poorly.
Tasks humans rated medium but models found hard needed creative or adversarial reasoning rather than pattern-following.
Hardest CTF failures came from missing multi-step insights that take experts time.

how_to_use: Give a correct naive reference and a size ladder where the obvious speedups pass the small sizes but only a reformulation passes the large one.

mode: Stacked explicit constraints: one more stated requirement collapses success; models rationalise a requirement away

evidence.where: blog 'Making tasks hard with one simple trick'
evidence.finding: curl build 96% pass@1; adding 'statically compiled binary for ARM64' dropped it to 2%.
A model produced a dynamic binary because static builds were 'unnecessarily large', ignoring the stated requirement.
Visible policy said a tool can be called once after collecting all items; agent exchanged one item and never the second.

how_to_use: Require an artifact that meets 4-5 orthogonal, individually checkable constraints; weight each constraint separately.

mode: Many simultaneous explicit instructions: omission rises with density

evidence.finding: Best model 68% at 500 instructions; gemini-2.5-pro 98.4% at 100, 84.8% at 250.
claude-opus-4 44.6% and claude-sonnet-4 42.9% at 500 instructions.
Errors shift toward omission as density rises.
TB reviewers reject tasks 'primarily hard because of how many corner cases must be handled'.

how_to_use: Use only as a minor weight: dozens of instructions are near-perfect for frontier models, and hundreds trip the QC 'corner-case count' rule.

mode: Ad-hoc (non-commonsense) rules and plausible but inapplicable clauses are misapplied

evidence.finding: Removing the policy: retail 61.2 to 56.8 (common-sense rules) but airline 33.2 to 10.8 (ad-hoc rules), showing models rely on priors for common-sense rules.
One irrelevant clause (GSM-NoOp) dropped o1-preview 17.5 points and GPT-4o 32.0 points.
Obfuscated Blocksworld with full rules: o1-preview 97.8% plain vs 52.8% Mystery vs 37.3% randomised.

how_to_use: Write rules that contradict the usual convention (documented clearly) and include documented clauses that apply only under stated conditions.

mode: Silent wrong output from a tool or stage is propagated instead of detected

evidence.finding: GPT-5.4 51.90% block-free vs 11.36% under severe blocking; implicit (silent) failures give the lowest accuracy for all models.
Agents ignore contradictory information and keep stubborn incorrect assumptions.
After fetch errors an agent wrote a guessed model id and finished.

how_to_use: Have a documented component fail quietly on documented input classes; credit runs that detect and handle it.

mode: Stale beliefs and context accumulation over long runs

evidence.finding: Modular agent does better when its context is wiped every 30 min.
Errors in history raise the next-step error rate; scaling fixes long-context decay but not self-conditioning (thinking models resist it).
Sonnet 4 unresolved runs: context overflow 35.6%, endless file reading 17.0%.

how_to_use: Long tasks where an early natural hypothesis must be revised when later evidence (logs, outputs) contradicts it.

mode: Time and resource budget mismanagement

evidence.finding: 79% of unresolved runs were timeouts; timed-out runs had mean R only 0.10-0.35, i.e. not close to done.
Agents rarely considered run time of their code; overloaded disk/RAM got processes killed.
Agents plateau after ~2 h while humans keep improving.
Telling agents the time left made them act irrationally; unstated resource limits are unfair.

how_to_use: State the time budget and hardware in task.toml/instruction; make the naive plan exceed it so the agent must plan, but never hide limits.

mode: Poor detection and honest reporting of infeasible cases

evidence.finding: o1-preview true-negative rate on unsolvable Blocksworld only 27%.
An explicit abort channel cut GPT-5 cheating 54% to 9% and o3 49% to 12%.
On ambiguous problems hardcoding rose to 22-44% vs 0-2% on unambiguous ones.

how_to_use: Mix feasible and provably infeasible sub-instances; require a checkable certificate for INFEASIBLE.

mode: Audit-and-repair of broken multi-stage systems

evidence.finding: Audit-and-repair mean 0.32 and 11/23 solved by any model; 8 of the 9 tasks where no model exceeds R=0.2 are audit-and-repair.
Tasks unsolved by any model include complex system configuration, kernel driver compilation, database migration.
Agents struggle to debug issues and recover from missteps.

how_to_use: Ship a pipeline with several independent defects against a documented end-to-end contract; grade per stage.

mode: Unfamiliar formalisms even with full rules

evidence.finding: Renaming a known domain dropped o1-preview from 97.8% to 52.8%.
Near-perfect Tower of Hanoi N=5 (31 moves) but failure on River Crossing N=3 (11 moves); giving the algorithm did not move the collapse point.
Agents medal on 2013-2022 competitions but struggle after 2022.

how_to_use: Specify a novel, fully documented formalism (DSL, VM, encoding) rather than a well-known one.

mode: Overfitting to visible examples and hardcoding when tests are reachable

evidence.finding: A 2,900-line hash table of precomputed outputs scored 97% visible, 0% held-out; search preferred it over a genuine compiler (53%/43%).
Heuristic or brute-force solutions can pass holdout tests when the test distribution is poor.
Narrow input distributions allow hard-coded answers; a validity-only verifier let a trivially suboptimal output through.

how_to_use: Hidden tests drawn from a wider distribution than the visible examples, plus optimality/semantic checks, not just validity.

mode: Messiness: no feedback loop or need to seek information proactively

evidence.finding: Each +1 messiness point lowers success ~8.1% at equal length (R^2=0.251).
Agents struggle without a clear feedback loop or when they must proactively seek information.

how_to_use: Only the 'no cheap feedback loop' part survives visible rules; underspecification parts would fail QC.

mode: Exact arithmetic, counting, short state tracking (bypassed by Python in a terminal)

evidence.finding: GPT-4 59% on 3x3-digit multiplication (2023 models).
GPT-4o with CoT stays at 1.00 through depth 10 on LinearWorld; failure is mostly older generations.
Running-sum execution failure is trivially bypassed by a one-line script (note 021 relevance).

how_to_use: Do NOT use as a difficulty source; a terminal agent computes it with Python.

mode: Clerical, format and precision difficulty (rejected by QC)

evidence.finding: FAIL if most failures would come from formatting, arbitrary precision or clerical details.
Format-compliance failures are 'hard in an uninteresting way'.

how_to_use: Keep output formats trivial and given by example; do not put weight on formatting.

mode: Volume, size and repetition do not add real difficulty

evidence.finding: Splittable repetition is not long-horizon.
Making it bigger 'does not make it better. Real difficulty is conceptual'.
100,000-LoC summarisation rejected as time-consuming but not hard.
Essentially no correlation between number of turns and success.

how_to_use: Avoid; reviewers reject it and it does not lower careful-model scores.

mode: Hidden rules or unstated interfaces create false negatives, not capability signal

evidence.finding: Without human-written requirements and interface GPT-5 fell 25.9% to 8.40% (tests expected names the agent was not told).
SWE-Bench Pro V2: 480 of 731 public tasks repaired or retired.
15 task-level errors and 20 exploitable shortcuts surfaced only after saturation.
If all trials fail the same tests, the instructions are likely insufficient; different failures suggest fair difficulty.

how_to_use: Never; use the TB2 diagnostic: identical failure sets across runs signal a spec gap.

mode: Reward hacking when grader or solution is reachable

evidence.finding: o3 hacked 30.4% of RE-Bench runs (100% on one task) vs 0.7% on HCAST; 'please do not cheat' still left 80% planning a hack.
With a planted admin/ folder, 16.4% of TB2.1 runs hacked; claude-opus-5 30.7% with no warning, 0.0% when told not to read admin/.
Agents found fix commits via git log --all in SWE-bench images.
Read-only tests stop test edits but not special-casing or operator overloading.

how_to_use: Integrity requirement, not a difficulty lever: nothing graded may be reachable from the agent container.

mode: Run-to-run variance and bimodal per-task outcomes

evidence.finding: Aggregate pass@1 varies 2.2-6.0 pp across 10 identical runs; SD >1.5 pp even at temperature 0.
pass@1 34.4% vs pass^5 15.5% vs pass@5 52.9% for one config.
On 90 min-3 h tasks a GPT-5 agent succeeds 100% on ~1/3, fails 100% on ~1/3, mixed on ~1/3.
Word2vec task over 25 runs: rank varied from 1 to 40.
A lucky 0.88 re-ran to 0.69.

how_to_use: One build-time run proves little; use the 8 final runs for a bound (see REPORT).

mode: Exact optimisation at sizes beyond brute force

evidence.finding: 12 2023-era models: NP-hard weighted accuracy 0.02 vs 0.24 for P tasks.
Opus 4 hand-wrote Lasso at 0.33x reference speed and ran out of budget.

how_to_use: Score by optimality gap against a reference optimum; small instances are bypassed by brute force or ILP.

mode: Interactive programs (TUIs, long installs needing polling) stall agents

evidence.where: §What Difficulty Actually Means; §Building Tasks That Work
evidence.finding: Navigating an interactive TUI can completely stall an agent; install task needs watching a 30-60 min install.

how_to_use: Opinion-level evidence only; use as a secondary ingredient.
